warning_texts: Both test claims store p as 0.0000000000 with display_digits 4, which renders as a p of exactly zero; the recomputed p values are around 1e-157 for completion and below double precision for AOV, so the release should show them as below a bound rather than as zero.

Both test claims name the bonferroni correction with alpha 0.05 but record no adjusted per-test alpha; with p far below any adjusted threshold the conclusion is unaffected, but the correction is named rather than shown applied.

The completion-rate caveats say 'orders in this channel' but do not state in words that cancelled and pending orders are in the denominator; the recount confirms they are (denominators 24597 and 19934 are every direct and partner order in the population).

Only claims_recomputed goes back to the raw export; recompute_estimate, recompute_test and min_group_size read clean_data/orders_clean.csv, and independent_claim_recalc.json covers the six non-test claims only. This auditor's recount from the quarantine projection agrees with all of them in this run

The check plan leaves the answers' caveat text and the AOV caveat topics unchecked by any machine rule, which is where both blockers of this stage sit; caveats_declared for CLM-AOV-* could require the delivered-only and net-of-refunds topics.

The two-channel differences are observational: country and month strata keep the same sign and similar size (completion gap 0.108 to 0.130, AOV gap 21.91 to 24.93 EUR), so neither country mix nor month explains them, but nothing in the data supports a causal reading of channel.
summary: All eight claims trace byte-for-byte to calculated_metrics.json and reproduce from quarantine/orders.csv under the spec's latest_revision_wins rule (points, Wilson/Student intervals, n, z/t statistics, effects), and plan fields (hypothesis_id, method, alpha, correction, level) match audit/analysis_plan.json; the effect sign holds in every country and month stratum.
